newsitem.title: USA: Airbus see exclusive pacts as "bad for business".
newsitem.headline: Airbus see exclusive pacts as "bad for business".

text.p: Airbus Industrie said it is not pursuing an exclusive supplier pact with Continental Airlines Inc and sees sole-supplier deals as "bad for business."
The European consortium, however, said it remains in active negotiations with Continental for a possible wide-body jet aircraft deal.

Houston-based Continental said earlier on Monday it is in talks with two manufacturers for a wide-body jet order. As part of those talks, Continental asked Boeing Co to submit additional details about possibly forging an exclusive supplier relationship, a Continental spokeswoman said.
Boeing has recently forged exclusive provider relationships with AMR Corp's American Airlines and Delta Air Lines Inc.
"They asked Boeing, in light of the last two deals. They have not asked that of us," said Airbus spokesman David Venz.
"We have never engaged in exclusive deals. We think it's bad for business. Airlines that go into that have to be aware of the apparent short-term gain in terms of long-term pain," Venz said.
Airbus also harshly criticized the recent Delta contract, saying it was "anti-competitive."

Airbus said Boeing has aggressively pursued exclusive contracts with some of its existing, major customers. Boeing negotiated for future aircraft orders, while also offering to renegotiate past contracts, Venz said.
Continental, Delta and American Airlines have mostly Boeing jets in their fleet.
Boeing officials could not be immediately reached for comment.
